say: I've been coming here fifty years and I've never seen it like this. Well. Maybe in 1982.
Don't mind me. I'm just an old so-and-so who remembers when things worked.
@how_are_things

options.text: I'm sorry. What would make it better?
It's an old building. Bear with us.
Rinks are hard. Take it or leave it.

say: Lumber Kings tonight. I've had the same seat since the opener. They'll carry me out of it.
{event}. We'll beat Kessler. We won't. But we'll talk about it all week.
I sat right here in 1979. Ronnie scored five. You should have heard the roof.

options.text: Tell me about 1979.
Enjoy the game.

say: Up with the birds. At my age, you don't sleep in. You wake up and check you did.
Morning! Legion coffee's at seven. I came here first. Don't tell the Legion.

options.text: Good to see you anyway.

say: Ah, {owner}. Sit a minute. Your knees are young, they'll forgive you.
There's the young owner. Gus would have liked you. He'd never say so.

options.text: Good to see you too, {known_as}.

say: @how_are_things
Well, what can I do for you?
I've got all the time in the world. That's the trouble with retirement.

options.text: What brings you back every week?
What brings you to the rink?
What do you make of the rink?
Any news around town?
What would make this place better for you?
Take care.

say: The hockey, the people, the clock that runs fast. Mostly the people. A bit the clock.
I came for the Lumber Kings in 1974 and I just never stopped. Nobody told me to.
My wife and I skated here on Fridays. Now I watch. It's still nice.

options.text: It wouldn't be the same without you.
Tell me a bit about yourself.
Glad you come.
Good to know you, {known_as}.

say: They don't make benches like this any more. Good thing too.
The clock's fast and the roof drips. But don't touch the clock.
@ice

options.text: The ice has been better lately, hasn't it?
Noticed the work on the building?
Fair enough. We're working on it.

say: Now that's ice. Gus would have had a little smile about that. Just a little one.
The ice is good again. I said it would be. I said it to nobody, but I said it.

options.text: Glad it shows.

say: Somebody put a rail on the stairs. My knees wrote you a thank-you note.
The lobby's lovely. You kept the mural. Good. Some things you keep.

options.text: That's the idea.

say: Irene Dubois is still doing Albert's laps as well as her own. Every week. Since he passed.
Stan Szymanski stood at that rail every home game since 1974. His elbows polished the steel.

options.text: Ha. Good to know.

say: A handrail on those steps would be nice. I'd like to keep my hips another year or two.
Rails on the stairs to the stands. We're not all spring chickens up there.

options.text: I'll see what I can do.
Can't promise anything, but noted.
You're not the first to say it. It's on the list.

say: Off you go. I'll be right here. Same as always.
Mind how you go. Mind the third step. It's been loose since 1988.
